hero.title: AEROSPACE ENGINEERING UNDERGRADUATE IN FRANCE
hero.subtitle: France is a popular destination for students interested in **studying aerospace engineering,** aviation technology, aircraft design, propulsion systems and space exploration.

overview: France is a popular destination for students interested in **studying aerospace engineering,** aviation technology, aircraft design, propulsion systems and space exploration.
The country has specialized engineering schools, applied science programs and ****bachelor’s degree pathways**** linked to **aerospace engineering**.

International students need to know about the French degree structure. Other institutions offer a 3-year bachelor’s degree and others a 5-year engineering programme** which leads to a recognized engineering qualification.
Students can get to know about these opportunities and the requirements for studying abroad with **Edu Hawk worldwide study abroad guidance.**

sections.title: 1. Can I do aerospace engineering in France after 12th?

items: Yes. Some institutions have **bachelor's-level programmes** or **five-year engineering pathways** from after secondary school. The entry requirements and structure of each program must be checked.

sections.title: 2. How many years of aerospace engineering in France?

items: A **bachelor’s programme** typically lasts three years. A **French engineering-school pathway** usually takes five years after secondary school, but students who already have some higher education may do a shorter part of the pathway.

sections.title: 3. FAQ Are there any aerospace engineering courses taught in English in France?

items: The **International Bachelor’s program at INSA Lyon** is one of the English-taught programs. Other programs may be taught in French or have language requirements for entry. Always check the current teaching language.

sections.title: 4. What is the salary of an aerospace engineer in France?

items: The tuition fees for aerospace engineering in France vary greatly. Public institutions may charge national tuition rates or differential fees, while private specialist schools charge their own fees. Living expenses are extra, and applicants should consult the official fee schedules for the latest information.

items: ****Accreditation and Degree Recognition**** These are also important when selecting an aerospace engineering program.

In France, the *Diplôme d’ingénieur* is a recognized engineering qualification if it is awarded by a program that is authorized by the relevant French authorities under the accreditation process of the **Commission des titres d’ingénieur (CTI)**.
Before you apply, make sure you:
* the type of degree awarded by the program (a **bachelor's degree**, a **licence grade** or a *Diplôme d’ingénieur*).
* Is the qualification officially recognized?
* Is the engineering program **currently accredited by CTI**, if applicable.
* The total number of **ECTS credits** and the length of the program.
* Recognition for further education or for professional recognition in your country of employment.

****Aerospace engineering graduates**** are qualified for positions in **aircraft manufacturing, aviation systems, space technology, engineering consulting, testing, simulation, and advanced materials**.
Possible ****aerospace engineering job opportunities**** are:
* - **Engineer of aerospace design.
* - **Flight mechanics or aerodynamics engineer
* - **Aircraft structures engineer**.
* - **Embedded systems and avionics engineer**.
* - **A satellite or space systems engineer.
* - Simulation Test engineer
* - Manufacturing engineer, quality engineer or production engineer
A graduate's job prospects are influenced by their degree level, technical skills, internships, language abilities and work authorization.
A three-year bachelor’s degree can be a stepping stone to further study, as many professional aerospace engineering jobs require a **engineering diploma or master’s-level education**.

****Aerospace engineering salary**** levels are dependent on employer, location, specialization and experience. But to compare apples with apples you need to look at current vacancies and salary surveys for the exact role and country you want to work in.
The **documents required for aerospace engineering applications in France** are usually:
- **Valid passport.
- Class 10 and Class 12 certificates and transcripts, as applicable.
- Evidence of **math and physics preparation**.
- Test results (in English or French), if applicable.
- Curriculum vitae, if required.
- **Letter of motivation or statement of purpose**, if applicable.
- **Letters of recommendation** if applicable.
- Certified translations of academic documents, if required.
- Application forms and/or payment of the application fees, if applicable.
- Additional **financial and visa documentation** where appropriate.
